mission_goal: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas Ubuntu developer system

zero_cost_evidence.claim: NVIDIA Developer Program members have free access to hosted NIM API endpoints for prototyping; individual endpoints may be rate limited.
zero_cost_evidence.counterhypothesis: A configured credential can belong to a different billing or production context; request execution must still stay on the documented integrate.api.nvidia.com developer endpoint and emit a receipt.

response_bounds.claim: A bounded read must request one sentinel byte beyond the accepted limit to distinguish an oversized response from a response that merely fills the limit.
response_bounds.counterhypothesis: Reading exactly the accepted limit is sufficient; falsified because HTTPResponse.read(amt) returns only up to amt bytes and therefore cannot prove end-of-body at that boundary.

text_message_roles.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; tool/function messages require the separate typed tool-calling path.
text_message_roles.counterhypothesis: An arbitrary nonempty role can be delegated to provider-side validation; falsified for this adapter because it causes an avoidable authenticated network call before the provider can reject it.

incomplete_body_errors.claim: http.client.IncompleteRead after a received response is an incomplete provider response, not an unhandled process exception.
incomplete_body_errors.counterhypothesis: Timeout handling covers every interrupted body read; falsified because IncompleteRead is an HTTPException rather than TimeoutError or URLError and escaped without a receipt.

pre_response_disconnects.claim: A ConnectionError such as http.client.RemoteDisconnected before response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
pre_response_disconnects.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps remote disconnects in URLError; falsified by the executable opener path where RemoteDisconnected escaped directly without a receipt.

malformed_http_status.claim: A BadStatusLine before valid response headers is an unreachable provider attempt with null status and no EXECUTED state.
malformed_http_status.counterhypothesis: Only timeout, URL and connection exceptions can occur before a response; falsified because BadStatusLine is an independent HTTPException and escaped without a receipt.

transport_os_errors.claim: Transport-layer OSError failures such as ssl.SSLError before response headers are unreachable provider attempts with null status and no EXECUTED state.
transport_os_errors.counterhypothesis: urllib always wraps TLS failures in URLError or ConnectionError; falsified by the executable opener path where SSLError propagated directly without a receipt.

http_status_validation.claim: A provider adapter must supply an integer HTTP status from 100 through 599 before the body is consumed or EXECUTED is asserted; missing, boolean, textual and out-of-range values are invalid.
http_status_validation.counterhypothesis: A missing adapter status can safely default to 200 and Python isinstance(value, int) is sufficient; falsified because missing status verified arbitrary content and bool is an int subclass.

http_response_body_type.claim: The HTTP adapter body must be bytes before JSON parsing; text and bytearray values are invalid transport responses even when they contain valid JSON.
http_response_body_type.counterhypothesis: Successful json.loads parsing proves a valid HTTP body; falsified because json.loads intentionally accepts str and bytearray in addition to bytes.

strict_json_numbers.claim: Provider response JSON containing NaN, Infinity or -Infinity is invalid and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
strict_json_numbers.counterhypothesis: Python json.loads success proves standards-compliant JSON; falsified because the default decoder accepts non-finite constants that RFC 8259 does not permit.

unique_json_object_names.claim: Provider response objects with duplicate member names are ambiguous across parsers and cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
unique_json_object_names.counterhypothesis: Python's last-name-wins behavior is a safe canonical interpretation; falsified as a portability claim because RFC 8259 documents error, last-only and all-pairs behaviors as interoperably unpredictable.

json_nesting_failure_receipts.claim: Excessively nested provider JSON that reaches Python's recursion limit must emit invalid_provider_response rather than escape without an execution receipt.
json_nesting_failure_receipts.counterhypothesis: The 2000000-byte response limit is sufficient to bound every JSON parser failure; falsified by a roughly 40000-byte, 20000-level array that raised RecursionError without a receipt.

unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.claim: Text-chat request and response strings must contain Unicode scalar values; lone UTF-16 surrogates cannot cross the authenticated request boundary or reach VERIFIED/DONE.
unicode_scalar_text_boundaries.counterhypothesis: Successful Python json.loads parsing proves an interoperable Unicode string; falsified because an escaped lone surrogate was decoded as str and reached success/VERIFIED/DONE even though RFC 8259 calls receiver behavior unpredictable.

plain_text_message_fields.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts exactly role and content in each message; tool_calls, tool_call_id, name, reasoning_content and future extension fields require an explicitly typed adapter.
plain_text_message_fields.counterhypothesis: Validating role and content is enough for a text-only adapter; falsified because an assistant message carrying tool_calls passed unchanged to the authenticated network opener.

invariants: Never serialize, log, commit, echo or display API secret values.
Never access Together, including discovery, probes, routing and fallback.
Never make a paid request unless the project owner separately authorizes a nonzero budget.
A configured key is capability evidence, not proof of quota or health.
Except for an officially documented free developer endpoint, a configured key requires explicit host-side zero-cost attestation before routing.
A provider credential may only be sent to that provider's canonical host; a global multi-provider host allowlist is forbidden.
Credential binding compares the full remote origin boundary, including the effective HTTPS port; hostname equality alone is insufficient.
Provider endpoint URLs containing userinfo are rejected before request construction or network access.
Authenticated provider requests must not follow HTTP redirects; redirects fail closed before credentials can cross an origin boundary.
The text-chat adapter validates a nonempty model plus object messages with nonempty string roles and string content before network access; typed multimodal requests require a separate adapter.
The text-chat adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; arbitrary and tool/function roles are rejected before routing, credential use or network access.
Each plain-text message contains exactly role and content; extension fields such as tool_calls are rejected before routing, credential use or network access and require a typed adapter.
Execution receipt request IDs bind provider, endpoint host and serialized request digest and remain stable across retries; attempt IDs are unique per execution attempt.
Attempt IDs include a fresh high-entropy nonce so equal-time concurrent attempts cannot alias; raw nonces are never serialized.
A response reaches VERIFIED only when choices is a non-empty list whose first message is an object with string content; malformed JSON shapes fail closed with a receipt.
An HTTP status response, including 429 and 5xx, proves EXECUTED transport but never VERIFIED or DONE; connection and timeout failures without an HTTP response remain unexecuted.
Every received non-2xx status remains unverified even when the transport returns it as a regular response object instead of raising HTTPError.
Before body consumption or EXECUTED, adapter status must be a non-boolean integer in the RFC 9110 range 100 through 599; missing or invalid values remain null and invalid_provider_response.
A received adapter body must be bytes before JSON parsing; text, bytearray and other body types remain EXECUTED with their valid status but cannot reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Provider response JSON is parsed with non-finite constants rejected; NaN, Infinity and -Infinity remain invalid_provider_response and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Every provider JSON object must have unique member names; duplicates remain invalid_provider_response and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
JSON parser RecursionError after a valid response remains EXECUTED with its status, emits invalid_provider_response, and never escapes the receipt path or reaches VERIFIED or DONE.
Text-chat model, role, request content and verified response content contain only Unicode scalar values; lone UTF-16 surrogates are rejected before network or VERIFIED/DONE.
Malformed bodies preserve the received HTTP status and classify as invalid_provider_response; connection or timeout failures without a response use null status and unreachable_provider.
ConnectionError failures before response headers, including RemoteDisconnected, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED.
HTTPException failures before valid response headers, including BadStatusLine, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED.

Transport OSError failures before response headers, including SSLError, emit an unreachable_provider receipt with null status and without EXECUTED; after response headers they preserve status and EXECUTED as incomplete_provider_response.
Once response headers and status are received, body-read failures preserve that status and EXECUTED while classifying as incomplete_provider_response; they never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
A truncated HTTP body raising IncompleteRead preserves the received status and EXECUTED, emits an incomplete_provider_response receipt, and never reaches VERIFIED or DONE.
Provider responses larger than 2000000 bytes are detected with a one-byte sentinel read, classified as provider_response_too_large, and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Every real provider request must emit a redacted execution receipt.
Rate limits and provider faults trigger bounded cooldown and rerouting, never retry storms.
